body:
Axis scales and peak markers on the spectrum plots, and a Complex I/Q Frequency Data Stream page. This description replaces my earlier per-build comments, which are superseded by it.

## What it changes

* **Axis scales** on Spectrum, Radio Astronomy and Signal Classifier: frequency in MHz and level in dB at every gridline, with axis titles. The labels are an overlay on the existing graticule (cursor, zoom and touch handling unchanged). The level is uncalibrated and the axis says `dB (uncal.)`, not dBm.
* **Peak markers** on Spectrum, Radio Astronomy (header field `PEAK ON/OFF`), Signal Classifier and the I/Q page: the two strongest bins of the visible window (the second at least 6 bins from the first, the DC/LO bins skipped), numbered on the trace, with frequency in MHz and level in dB in a readout at the top left.
* **Complex I/Q Frequency Data Stream** (new page, route `complexiq`): the `/iq-waterfall` channel of maia-httpd (maia-sdr PR 12, not in upstream yet; without it the page shows `disconnected`). A switch selects the view: magnitude (dB) and phase (-pi to +pi rad) over frequency; real and imaginary part, normalised to the unit circle (or raw LSB); Bode plot (dB and unwrapped phase over log frequency offset); Smith chart (bins normalised to the strongest, coloured by frequency). Bin number scale on top, readout line, Hold button.
* **dB scale fix (behaviour change, please review).** The `/waterfall` bins are power (two tones 12 dB apart in amplitude arrive 17.7 times apart), but the Spectrum, Radio Astronomy and Classifier pages converted them with 20*log10, so level differences were shown twice as large (24.6 dB for 12.4 dB). They now use 10*log10; the default REF is 100 (was 130) and the REF unit reads dB. Bins above REF are marked on the plot, with the peak value (`OVER REF`). If the old scale was deliberate, this is the one change I would drop.
* **Radio Astronomy frequency switching (FSW) fix.** After each retune the first frame that arrives still shows the old LO (the MQTT retune itself takes 130 to 220 ms). Two frames after each flip are now dropped (`fswSkipRef`). A strong tone gave only about +7 dB in SIG - REF at INTEG 5 s; it now gives +74 dB, a weak line +17.6 dB (was +16.2 dB). The Radio Astronomy auto scale outlier filter was adjusted to the new -100 dB clamp.

## Tested

Original Pluto and Pluto+ over a cabled 40 dB link at 2.4 GHz, Chrome, with known signals (one or two tones of different amplitude, the second at a quarter of the amplitude, 12.04 dB lower) and an independent Python decode of the same stream. Final test on firmware images built from this branch as rebased onto upstream main (a304a1f) (Pluto flashed from the .frm, Pluto+ from the SD image; both serve the page from the image, identical to a fresh bundle of the source). The full RF suite (I/Q check, phase check and frame phase check at 2.5, 10, 20, 30.72 and 61.44 MS/s on both boards; the check scripts are in maia-sdr PR 12) was run on two builds of the final branch state; the dashboard bundle in both is byte-identical (the second build differs only in documentation), and both runs gave 30 steps, 70 checks ok, 0 FAIL, every settings restore matched. Over the two runs: frame rotation measured minus predicted -0.0009 to +0.0023 rad (scatter at most 0.0019 rad), OFDM log correlation 0.987 to 0.999, phase derived frequency within -12.2 to +2.9 Hz of the time-domain one, phase model error at most 1.02 deg and 0.30 dB, I/Q against raw at most 13.9 deg. The FSW, CAL and view results below were measured on pages served by these images or by the first of the two builds.

* Browser peak equals the decode on both boards, for example Pluto+ at 2.5 MS/s: bins 3311 and 3344, 2400.770874 and 2400.791016 MHz, 65.1 and 52.7 dB, both in page and decode. The level difference of the two tones is 12.3 to 12.4 dB on the Spectrum page and in the decode.
* Real/Imaginary, Bode and Smith values recomputed from the page's own magnitude and phase readout agree to 0.001 (for example second tone 0.164 + j0.176 read, 0.164 + j0.175 computed).
* A synthetic stream with known content (low-pass) matches in the Bode view to 0.1 dB and 0.1 degree.
* Radio Astronomy CAL: ratio near 0 dB with the transmitter off, +78 dB on the tone afterwards (Pluto+ page). FSW with the fix, INTEG 30 s, both boards' own pages: strong tones P1 +74.2 dB and P2 +62.3 dB (Pluto+) and +71.4 dB and +60.1 dB (Pluto), mirror lines about -72 dB; weak line (about 10 dB above the noise) +17.6 dB (Pluto+). Strong tones on the Pluto+ page at INTEG 5 s: P1 +73.1 dB, P2 +61.5 dB; at INTEG 1 s: +73.3 dB and +61.6 dB (before the fix about +7 dB at 5 s and unusable at 1 s). Weak line (about 10 dB above the noise) at INTEG 1 s, one clean frame per dwell: +17.3 to +17.6 dB over 20 s, flat baseline within about 1.5 dB.
* Peak markers on the board-served Pluto Spectrum page: 2400.869565 MHz 93.3 dB and 2400.891549 MHz 81.3 dB, decode 2400.869141 and 2400.888672 MHz (page frequency about 0.4 kHz above the decode, below one bin), level difference 12.0 dB against 12.04 dB sent.

## Not tested / limits

Chrome only, no touch; other boards (the page needs the I/Q channel of maia-sdr PR 12); FSW on the Pluto's page at INTEG other than 30 s; the Bode phase of a single tone only shows window leakage (meaningful for a broadband stimulus); peak markers in CAL/FSW mode mark the strongest ratio bins; a signal exactly at the LO is not marked; the page frequency is about 0.4 kHz above the decode at 10 MS/s (below one bin, the cursor and axes share the mapping). Plots outside these pages (signal generator, Webtioune, overview) are unchanged.

Test notes, tables, scripts (including `test/lag.py`, which measures the stale frames behind the FSW fix) and 57 screenshots: `Dashboard/docs/complex-iq/README.md`, written as one final test report, not per build. The branch is one commit, rebased onto upstream main (a304a1f).
